title: Add /chunklock database command for MySQL status
description: Admin command to check active storage backend, MySQL connection pool status, and trigger operations
user_note: Added '/chunklock database' command to view storage backend status (MapDB or MySQL) with connection pool metrics, performance stats, and migration status
notes: Provides visibility into MySQL vs MapDB usage, connection health, and pool statistics

title: Create comprehensive MySQL setup documentation
description: Dedicated guide covering MySQL installation, configuration, migration, and troubleshooting
user_note: Created comprehensive MySQL Setup Guide with step-by-step instructions for server setup, configuration, migration, performance tuning, and troubleshooting
notes: Should include complete step-by-step setup, performance tuning, and common issues

title: Update admin commands documentation with database command
description: Add database status command documentation to Admin-Commands.md wiki page
user_note: Updated Admin Commands documentation with comprehensive /chunklock database command reference including example outputs for both MapDB and MySQL modes
notes: Integrate with existing admin commands documentation

title: Enhance debug command to show MySQL connection details
description: Update /chunklock debug output to include MySQL-specific metrics when MySQL is active
user_note: Added '/chunklock debug database' subcommand showing connection status, query performance, and pool statistics for MySQL or file sizes for MapDB
notes: Show connection pool stats, active connections, query performance if MySQL mode

title: Fix resource-based unlock: players stuck without required materials
description: Players spawning in chunks without biome-required materials (e.g., Plains with no trees) could not progress. Added resource-scan cost mode that bases unlock costs on materials actually available in the player's owned chunks. Fixed GUI display/validation mismatch where biome items were shown but PaymentRequirement items were validated. Fixed items never being consumed on material unlock.
user_note: Added new 'resource-scan' cost mode that scans your owned chunks and only requires materials you can actually gather. Fixed unlock GUI showing wrong material requirements and items not being consumed on unlock.
notes: Enable with materials.cost-mode: 'resource-scan' in economy.yml. Falls back to biome-based if scan returns no resources. Scans cached per-player with configurable TTL.

title: Fix false insufficient-material unlock failures
description: Fix regression where vanilla material unlock checks could fail despite sufficient inventory and show incorrect missing amounts.
user_note: Fixed a regression where chunk unlock could fail even when you had enough vanilla materials in inventory. Missing-item messages now show correct non-negative values.
notes: GitHub issue: #71

title: Restore single-resource requirement in materials mode
description: Material unlocks were enforcing multiple biome resources at once in some flows. Restored single-resource requirement behavior for affordability and payment consistency.
user_note: Materials unlock now requires one resource again (not multiple at once), matching legacy behavior and expected gameplay.
notes: Keeps first vanilla requirement when biome defines multiple entries.

title: Fix MySQL starting chunk reassignment after restart
description: After server restart, players could be assigned a new starting chunk because in-memory claims were empty and persisted spawn ownership was not restored in SingleWorldManager. Claim lookup now restores from persisted player spawn data before assigning a new chunk.
user_note: Fixed issue where /chunklock start could give a new chunk after restart on MySQL. Existing persisted claim is now restored and reused.
notes: GitHub issue: #65

title: Reduce repeated acacia costs and improve material cost scaling
description: Resource-scan was over-selecting wood/acacia and flattening costs around fixed values due to strict availability capping.
user_note: Improved resource-scan variety and progression scaling: repeated wood/acacia picks are reduced and costs no longer flatten around fixed values during progression.
notes: GitHub issue: #76

title: Harden resource-scan pricing against scarcity exploits and improve consistency
description: Reworked resource-scan to use deterministic candidate sorting, weighted wood de-prioritization, diminishing-return progression scaling, and a bounded soft availability modifier instead of hard availability caps.
user_note: Resource-scan now selects materials more consistently and fairly, prevents low-cost scarcity exploits, and shows players that prices are based on claimed-chunk resources.
notes: GitHub issue: #77

title: Fix NoSuchElementException in ResourceBasedMaterialStrategy during async cost calculation
description: The recent-selection history added for #77 used a plain HashMap of ArrayDeque, but calculateRequirement runs on async threads via AsyncCostCalculationService (runTaskAsynchronously and two CompletableFuture.supplyAsync call sites). Concurrent trimming could call removeFirst() on an empty deque and throw NoSuchElementException, and the unsynchronized HashMap risked corruption under concurrent computeIfAbsent. Switched to ConcurrentHashMap + ConcurrentLinkedDeque and replaced removeFirst() with pollFirst(), which returns null instead of throwing. Also added per-player cleanup on quit so the map does not grow unbounded on long-running servers.
user_note: Fixed an error that could occur while calculating unlock costs in resource-scan mode, which could cause the unlock menu to fail to open or show incorrect requirements.
tests: Regression verified: reverting pollFirst() to removeFirst() makes the new concurrency test fail with NoSuchElementException
notes: GitHub issue: #78. Root cause was introduced by the #77 work in the same file, so both ship together.

title: Bound the hologram state cache
description: Hologram state map grew without bound: 5 puts, 0 individual removes, clear() only on shutdown, and the periodic cleanup task was an empty stub. Added a stale-entry eviction policy plus a hard cap.
user_note: The hologram state cache no longer grows without bound during exploration; stale entries are evicted and the cache is hard-capped
tests: HologramStateEvictionTest: 6 passed. Verified they catch the defect - disabling eviction fails 4 of 6, retaining 2000 entries vs ~540
notes: GitHub issue: #74. Locally validated Aug 29; cache plateaus as designed. Issue stays OPEN pending real-load data - the 64GB report from a heavily modified server at high player count was not reproduced.

title: Add /chunklock debug memory
description: Surfaces hologram cache counters in chat rather than a raw stats map on the console, for validating the #74 eviction fix on a live server.
user_note: New '/chunklock debug memory' command showing hologram cache totals, evictions and usage percentage
notes: The number to watch is cached-despawned: it should plateau while exploring, not climb.

title: Stop the unlock GUI re-rolling the required material
description: calculateRequirement read like a query but called rememberSelection, and computeSelectionScore penalises recent selections by -350. Against a four-candidate window this produced a strict 4-cycle - the reported gravel/clay/sand/dirt rotation - from ten pure-display call sites.
user_note: The unlock menu no longer changes the required material each time you open it
notes: GitHub issue: #82. PR #85.

title: Make chunk prices a commitment, with a priced re-roll
description: Persistence already existed but only TraditionalVaultStrategy called storeCost. Wired the resource-scan path through it, keyed per (player, chunk, config hash), plus a re-roll service with a 1h per-chunk cooldown or escalating Vault cost. GUI button at slot 33.
user_note: Once you have seen a price for a chunk it is honoured until you pay it or re-roll it, surviving relog, restart and cache expiry. New re-roll button for a different requirement
notes: GitHub issue: #83. PR #89. Play-testing found the re-roll charging without changing the requirement (46f44c2) and offering itself when only one candidate existed (f73a61d, PR #93).

title: Do not offer a re-roll that cannot change anything
description: Selection is deterministic, so a player whose territory yields exactly one obtainable material paid for an impossibility. GUI and payment path now both read EconomyManager.hasRerollAlternatives.
user_note: The re-roll button is greyed out, with the reason shown, when a re-roll could not change anything
notes: GitHub issue: #83. PR #93. Not yet play-tested.

title: Price chunks from their own contents
description: Replaces owned-chunk aggregate pricing with per-chunk profiling: profile capture on the main thread, a persisted running material baseline, a distinctiveness metric (surface-weighted, relative to baseline), and the #69 obtainability ladder wired into ResourceBasedMaterialStrategy. Prototype measured raw abundance at 1-of-5 distinct chunks vs 5-of-5 for the chosen metric.
user_note: A chunk's cost is now based on what is in that chunk. Forests ask for wood, mountains andesite, deserts sand - and two adjacent chunks with different terrain price differently
tests: 145 tests total, up from 35 when the work began
Verified to catch a raw-abundance revert (4 failures) and a removed tier cap (3)
notes: GitHub issue: #86. PRs #94, #100, #102. Changes what every chunk costs and resets servers mid-progression - this is why the release is 2.3.0 and not 2.2.1.

title: Honour the distinctiveness ranking when selecting a material
description: Candidates were re-scored as tier*1000+count - correct for the owned-chunk pool, wrong for the target-chunk pool. Below 3 unlocked chunks it produced a dirt/gravel/clay rotation; from 3 onward every chunk would have priced as stone.
user_note: Chunk prices favour what makes a chunk distinctive rather than what it holds the most of
tests: selectForPool pins the routing at the call site
notes: GitHub issue: #86. Found by play-testing, not by 128 passing tests. Would have shipped.

title: Actually count unlocked chunks, and repair worlds where it never was
description: Nothing ever called incrementUnlockedChunks; a comment claiming otherwise described a call that did not exist. Every player read 0 forever, so getMaxTierForProgression(0) capped candidates at tier 3 and the progression cost multiplier stayed flat. getUnlockedChunkCount now treats 0 as never-tallied and recomputes once from the chunk database.
user_note: Unlocked chunks are now actually counted; existing worlds recount themselves once from stored chunk ownership
notes: Predates #86 entirely. Reported by the owner as an aside while describing a different symptom - the aside was the cause.

title: Stop featureless chunks pricing themselves in deepslate
description: The metric could say what a chunk was most above average in, but never whether it was distinctive at all. On a bland chunk every score hovers near 1.0 and the top entry wins by noise - and bulk depth stone is the noisiest candidate. Added a distinctiveness margin plus a filler discount.
user_note: A chunk with no real character falls back to territory-based pricing instead of picking a material at random
notes: GitHub issue: #86. Owner chose discount-not-ban so a genuine mountainside at 2.5x still headlines. DISTINCTIVENESS_MARGIN is 1.3 and unmeasured in practice - worth a play observation.

title: Key the chunk cost MERGE on the unique constraint
description: storeCost used a bare MERGE INTO, which H2 keys on the PRIMARY KEY - the auto-increment id the statement never supplies - so every write failed with 90081 and chunk_costs was empty on every server.
user_note: Chunk costs are now written to the database at all. Every write had been failing silently
tests: ChunkCostPersistenceTest runs real H2; verified it fails with 90081 without the fix. 62 tests passing
notes: GitHub issue: #90. PR #92. Live-verified: console spam gone.

title: Route chunk cost and profile storage on database.type
description: Not a connection swap - the SQL was H2-only and would fail on every MySQL write, and the || concat would have failed SILENTLY. Added SqlDialect and CostStorageBackend. Also fixed a latent #78-shaped threading bug.
user_note: Chunk cost and profile storage now follow your configured database.type. On multi-server MySQL setups, prices no longer diverge per node
tests: SqlDialectTest across 4 nested classes. 98 tests passing
notes: GitHub issue: #95. PR #96. Owner confirmed on a live MySQL server that chunks_counted matches the distinct chunk count on every baseline row, so the silent || collapse did not occur.

title: Resolve message keys added after a server first start
description: LanguageManager writes lang/en.yml only when absent, and nothing reconciled an existing file with the jar copy. Any key added by a later update was missing and getMessage returned the raw key. Fixed with setDefaults plus copyDefaults(false), so admin edits keep priority and their file is never rewritten.
user_note: Messages added by plugin updates now display correctly on servers first started on an earlier version, instead of rendering as raw keys
notes: General, not specific to #83 - affects every message added since a given server first started.

title: Stop players spawning in the void after /chunklock start
description: Two defects. findValidStartingChunk ran async and called world.getChunkAt, which off the main thread returns an ungenerated chunk, so every height lookup reported world minimum and clamped spawn to Y=-63. And SingleWorldManager stored the claim in memory only, never calling setChunk, so respawn found no saved spawn.
user_note: Players no longer spawn in the void after '/chunklock start', and the assigned spawn is saved so dying does not drop you back into it
notes: Also explains the 'Can't keep up! Running 6776ms behind' warning in the same log - async chunk access forcing sync main-thread work.

title: Warn clearly when holograms are enabled but no provider loads
description: A single INFO line conflated a deliberate disable with a failed provider load. Now a failed provider prints a warning block naming the provider, whether the plugin is present, where to download it, and the Java-version pitfall. isProviderDisabled is now case-insensitive.
user_note: When holograms are enabled but the provider fails to load, the log now names the provider and what to check instead of one info line that scrolled past
notes: Prompted by a server running without holograms for a whole session: FancyHolograms was built for a newer Java, so the server skipped it silently. Also corrected README and Troubleshooting docs that claimed a nonexistent internal fallback.

title: Documentation truth pass
description: Removed the fossil dependency-reduced-pom.xml stale at 1.2.7 and gitignored it, fixed the README install comment, and dated docs/project-charter.md stating its gaps rather than rewriting it. Also rewrote the SpigotMC resource-scan copy to match the implementation.
user_note: Documentation no longer advertises behaviour the plugin does not have
notes: PR #99. The charter's '500 licenses at 89 dollars' line was a revenue projection later mistaken for fact - Chunklock is free. SpigotMC-Description.md is UTF-16 LE with BOM.

title: Replace stock issue templates and document triage
description: The bug template was GitHub's web-app boilerplate asking for iPhone model and browser version. Replaced with server software, Java version, cost strategy, hologram provider, storage backend and console output, plus a separate performance template. Label scheme documented in TRIAGE.md.
user_note: Issue templates now ask for the details a Minecraft plugin bug actually needs
notes: #74 showed performance reports need different information than functional bugs.
